title: RI S2195: Creates additional safety features for AI companion technology that include addressing suicidal ideation, potential physical harm or financial harm to others expressed by a user. It also requires notification the AI companion does not have human emotions.

obligations: An operator must ensure the AI companion contains a protocol for addressing possible suicidal ideation or self harm expressed by a user to the AI companion (6-63-2(a)(1)).
An operator must ensure the AI companion contains a protocol for addressing possible physical harm to others expressed by a user to the AI companion (6-63-2(a)(2)).

When any of those expressions are made, the operator must provide a notification to the user that refers them to crisis service providers such as a suicide hotline, crisis text line, or other appropriate crisis services as soon as any of those expressions are detected (6-63-2(a)(3)).
Beginning July 1, 2027, operators must file annual reports with the office of the attorney general including the number of safety protocol activations and related metrics (6-63-2(b)).

An operator must provide a clear and conspicuous notification to a user at the beginning of any AI companion interaction and at least every three hours for continuing AI companion interactions, stating either verbally or in writing that the user is not communicating with a human (6-63-3).
prohibitions: It is unlawful for any operator to operate or provide an AI companion to a user unless the AI companion contains the required protocols for addressing suicidal ideation or self harm and physical harm to others (6-63-2(a)).

What it does

This chapter requires operators of AI companions to include safety protocols for addressing user expressions of suicidal ideation, self harm, or physical harm to others, and to notify users that they are not communicating with a human. It also requires annual reporting to the attorney general and authorizes civil penalties for violations.

Who it applies to

  • Operators of AI companions as defined in 6-63-1(6)

Effective date

January 1, 2027

Key definitions

  • AI companion: a system using artificial intelligence, generative artificial intelligence, and/or emotional recognition algorithms to simulate a sustained human or human-like relationship with a user by retaining information on prior interactions or user sessions and user preferences to personalize the interaction and facilitate ongoing engagement; asking unprompted or unsolicited emotion-based questions that go beyond a direct response to a user prompt; and sustaining an ongoing dialogue concerning matters personal to the user. Excludes systems used solely for customer service or strictly providing information about available commercial services or products, customer service account information, or other information strictly related to customer service; systems primarily designed and marketed for providing efficiency improvements or research or technical assistance; and systems used solely for internal purposes or employee productivity (6-63-1(1)).
  • AI model: a component of an information system that implements artificial intelligence technology and uses computational, statistical, or machine-learning techniques to produce outputs from a given set of inputs (6-63-1(2)).
  • Artificial intelligence, artificial intelligence technology, or AI: a machine-based system that can, for a given set of human-defined objectives, make predictions, recommendations, or decisions influencing real or virtual environments (6-63-1(3)).
  • Emotional recognition algorithms: artificial intelligence that detects and interprets human emotional signals in text (using natural language processing and sentiment analysis), audio (using voice emotion AI), video (using facial movement analysis, gait analysis, or physiological signals), or a combination thereof (6-63-1(4)).
  • Generative artificial intelligence: a class of AI models that are self-supervised and emulate the structure and characteristics of input data to generate derived synthetic content including, but not limited to, images, videos, audio, text, and other digital content (6-63-1(5)).
  • Operator: any person, partnership, association, firm, or business entity, or any member, affiliate, subsidiary or beneficial owner of any partnership, association, firm, or business entity who operates or provides an AI companion (6-63-1(6)).
  • Person: any natural person (6-63-1(7)).
  • User: any person who uses an AI companion within the state and who is not an operator or agent or affiliate of the operator of the AI companion (6-63-1(8)).

Obligations

  • An operator must ensure the AI companion contains a protocol for addressing possible suicidal ideation or self harm expressed by a user to the AI companion (6-63-2(a)(1)).
  • An operator must ensure the AI companion contains a protocol for addressing possible physical harm to others expressed by a user to the AI companion (6-63-2(a)(2)).
  • When any of those expressions are made, the operator must provide a notification to the user that refers them to crisis service providers such as a suicide hotline, crisis text line, or other appropriate crisis services as soon as any of those expressions are detected (6-63-2(a)(3)).
  • Beginning July 1, 2027, operators must file annual reports with the office of the attorney general including the number of safety protocol activations and related metrics (6-63-2(b)).
  • An operator must provide a clear and conspicuous notification to a user at the beginning of any AI companion interaction and at least every three hours for continuing AI companion interactions, stating either verbally or in writing that the user is not communicating with a human (6-63-3).

Prohibitions

  • It is unlawful for any operator to operate or provide an AI companion to a user unless the AI companion contains the required protocols for addressing suicidal ideation or self harm and physical harm to others (6-63-2(a)).

Penalties and enforcement

The attorney general is empowered to enforce this chapter, including the power to investigate, sue, and seek injunctions against noncompliant AI companion operators (6-63-4(a)). Violations may result in civil penalties up to fifteen thousand dollars ($15,000) per day, with fines directed to suicide prevention programs (6-63-4(b)). No private right of action is stated in the text.

How it affects AI deployment

  • An organisation deploying an AI companion in Rhode Island must build in protocols to detect and respond to user expressions of suicidal ideation, self harm, or physical harm to others before offering the product (6-63-2(a)(1)-(2)).
  • The organisation must automatically provide a crisis service referral notification to the user when such expressions are detected (6-63-2(a)(3)).
  • The organisation must provide a clear and conspicuous notice at the start of each interaction and at least every three hours that the user is not communicating with a human (6-63-3).
  • The organisation must track safety protocol activations and related metrics and file annual reports with the attorney general beginning July 1, 2027 (6-63-2(b)).
  • Noncompliance can result in civil penalties up to $15,000 per day (6-63-4(b)).
  • The organisation should assess whether its product falls within the AI companion definition and is not excluded as customer service, efficiency/research/technical assistance, or internal/employee productivity use (6-63-1(1)(ii)).

Notable exemptions

  • AI companion does not include any system used by a business entity solely for customer service or to strictly provide users with information about available commercial services or products provided by such entity, customer service account information, or other information strictly related to its customer service (6-63-1(1)(ii)(A)).
  • AI companion does not include any system that is primarily designed and marketed for providing efficiency improvements or research or technical assistance (6-63-1(1)(ii)(B)).
  • AI companion does not include any system used by a business entity solely for internal purposes or employee productivity (6-63-1(1)(ii)(C)).

Compliance steps

  • Determine whether the product meets the definition of AI companion and is not excluded under 6-63-1(1)(ii).
  • Implement protocols to detect expressions of suicidal ideation or self harm and physical harm to others (6-63-2(a)(1)-(2)).
  • Implement a notification to the user referring them to crisis service providers when such expressions are detected (6-63-2(a)(3)).
  • Implement a clear and conspicuous notification at the beginning of each interaction and at least every three hours that the user is not communicating with a human (6-63-3).
  • Establish internal tracking of safety protocol activations and related metrics for annual reporting (6-63-2(b)).
  • File annual reports with the office of the attorney general beginning July 1, 2027 (6-63-2(b)).
  • Monitor compliance to avoid civil penalties up to $15,000 per day (6-63-4(b)).
